universities.name: London South Bank University
universities.summary: London South Bank University is a public university in south London with roots in the Borough Polytechnic Institute, founded in 1892. Its Southwark-based BSc (Hons) Computer Science is a three-year September course with a BCS accreditation shown on the course page and a four-year sandwich route that includes a placement year.
universities.campusLifestyle: The Computer Science course is taught at LSBU's Southwark campus. The university's computing school identifies facilities and learning around software, operating systems, high-performance computing and Raspberry Pi devices; the course page also lists work in programming, databases, AI, cloud computing and mobile development.
universities.cityProfile: LSBU's Southwark campus places students in central London, but the city needs a realistic budget. LSBU's current 2025/26 planning guide estimates a 39-week undergraduate year at £12,600–£18,400 in university accommodation or £16,400–£25,500 in private accommodation; those totals include more than rent and are not tuition charges.
universities.practicalExposure: The BSc course page describes hands-on work with programming, software development, databases and computing systems, and offers a four-year sandwich option with a work-placement year. It also cites past student projects for Southwark Council and RICS. These examples show the type of applied work associated with the course, not a guaranteed placement or employer outcome.
universities.hostelOverview: LSBU has two halls with more than 900 single bedrooms within a ten-minute walk of its main campus. For 2026/27, McLaren House publishes weekly rents from £215 for an ensuite to £295 for a superior ensuite with a large bed, with internet, utilities and contents insurance included; availability and room allocation are separate from a course offer.
universities.dietarySupport: LSBU's current cost guide budgets £45–£65 a week for food and household shopping. It does not publish a compulsory meal plan for Computer Science students. Campus microwaves are available in the Student Centre and LSBU Hub for students bringing food from home.
universities.safetyOverview: LSBU directs students to its SafeZone app for campus emergencies, first-aid requests and contact with the local safety team or a safety escort after dark. Its published emergency number is 020 7815 6666; immediate danger still requires the UK emergency number, 999.
universities.studentSupport: The Student Life Centre provides advice through appointments, online chat and MyAccount. LSBU lists specialist support for disability and dyslexia, money advice, employability, health and wellbeing, while international applicants can contact the university's dedicated international team before applying and after receiving an offer.
whyChoose: The BSc (Hons) Computer Science course page shows BCS accreditation and a curriculum spanning programming, databases, AI, cloud computing and mobile development.
Applicants can choose a three-year full-time route or a four-year sandwich route with a work-placement year.
The 2026/27 course page publishes the international annual fee and an illustrative total based on the current fee, allowing a clear first budget comparison.
LSBU publishes current international scholarships, including a £2,000-per-year Vice-Chancellor's International Merit Award for qualifying undergraduate applicants.
thingsToConsider: The £17,880 international fee is for 2026/27 entry and LSBU states that fees can rise annually; the displayed three-year total is based on the current annual fee rather than a fixed future-fee guarantee.
London living costs are material: LSBU's 39-week planning estimate is £12,600–£18,400 in university accommodation and £16,400–£25,500 privately, separate from tuition.

The standard full-time programme begins in September. International students needing a UK Student visa should apply full-time; LSBU says part-time study may not be available to those requiring that visa.
The course requires 112 UCAS points and GCSE Mathematics grade 4/C or an equivalent qualification; international equivalence must meet LSBU's published country and English-language requirements.
bestFitFor: Applicants seeking a London-based undergraduate Computer Science degree with a published three-year route and an optional sandwich placement year.
Students whose academic record meets the course's stated 112-UCAS-point and Mathematics-equivalent entry threshold.

faq.question: Is London South Bank University a public university?
faq.answer: Yes. LSBU is a public university in London with roots dating to the Borough Polytechnic Institute in 1892. It is listed in Office for Students fee information under UKPRN 10004078.

faq.question: Is the LSBU Computer Science degree accredited?
faq.answer: The current BSc (Hons) Computer Science course page shows BCS accreditation. LSBU's published course specification describes BCS accreditation for the academic requirements associated with Chartered IT Professional registration; professional registration itself remains subject to BCS requirements.

faq.question: How long is BSc Computer Science at LSBU?
faq.answer: The standard full-time BSc (Hons) Computer Science route is three years and starts in September. LSBU also lists a four-year sandwich route, which includes a work-placement year, and a four-year part-time route.

faq.question: What is the international tuition fee for Computer Science?
faq.answer: For 2026/27 entry, LSBU publishes an international annual tuition fee of £17,880 for the full-time BSc (Hons) Computer Science route. Its displayed three-year total is £53,640, calculated from the current annual fee and subject to future fee increases.

faq.question: What are the entry requirements for Computer Science?
faq.answer: LSBU lists 112 UCAS points and GCSE Mathematics at grade 4/C or equivalent for the course. International applicants should use LSBU's international qualification guidance to establish the equivalent school qualification and English-language evidence for their country.

faq.question: How do international applicants apply?
faq.answer: International applicants and EU applicants without settled or pre-settled status can apply directly to LSBU. The Computer Science page directs them to LSBU's international application guidance; applicants should submit the academic and identity evidence requested for their route.

faq.question: When does the course start and what is the 2026 application timing?
faq.answer: The full-time course starts in September. LSBU's undergraduate guidance says applicants for September 2026 should apply by 30 June 2026 to be considered before Clearing, while noting that course-specific deadlines can vary.

faq.question: Can international students receive an LSBU scholarship?
faq.answer: LSBU lists the Vice-Chancellor's International Merit Award at £2,000 per academic year for qualifying undergraduate international students with grades equivalent to AAB, approximately 75% or above in other international school-leaving certificates. It also lists a Global Success Scholarship of up to £4,000 in the first year, subject to the published conditions.

faq.question: What should I budget for accommodation and living in London?
faq.answer: LSBU's 2025/26 guide estimates £12,600–£18,400 for a 39-week undergraduate year in university accommodation and £16,400–£25,500 privately. For 2026/27, McLaren House rooms are published from £215 to £295 per week, with utilities, internet and contents insurance included.

faq.question: What student support is available at LSBU?
faq.answer: The Student Life Centre provides appointments, online chat and access to specialist teams. LSBU lists disability and dyslexia support, money advice, employability and wellbeing services, and its SafeZone app can contact campus safety staff or request a safety escort after dark.
